---
title: "Hydroclimate2k analysis tutorials"
subtitle: "Worked examples with the LiPD family of R packages"
---

These tutorials show how to analyze the [Hydroclimate2k](https://lipdverse.org/hydroclimate2k/) compilation in R, using the LiPD family of packages. They were written for the Hydroclimate2k workshop at UBC, Vancouver (November 9 to 11, 2026), but work for anyone.

Each tutorial runs from a fresh R session and reads the compilation from a local copy, so once you have run the setup step you can work offline.

## Start here

1. Follow **[Before the workshop](setup.qmd)**: install the packages and download the data (about 280 MB). Please do this before you arrive, because conference wifi will not cope with a room full of people downloading at once.
2. Work through the tutorials in order. Tutorial 1 introduces the data and the helper functions the others use.

## Tutorials

| | Tutorial | Packages |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | [Loading, exploring, plotting and mapping](tutorials/01-load-plot-map.qmd) | lipdR, lipdViz |
| 2 | [Regional composites](tutorials/02-compositeR.qmd) | compositeR |
| 3 | [Age uncertainty](tutorials/03-geoChronR.qmd) | geoChronR (agemodelR, ens, lipdViz) |
| 4 | [Detecting abrupt change](tutorials/04-actR.qmd) | actR |

## The packages

The LiPD family was reorganized and synchronized in November 2026. geoChronR is now a thin wrapper that loads four smaller packages:

| Package | What it does |
|---|---|
| [lipdR](https://github.com/nickmckay/lipdR) | Read, write, extract and filter LiPD data |
| [ens](https://github.com/nickmckay/ens) | Ensembles, binning, time-axis conversion, age-uncertain correlation and regression |
| [lipdViz](https://github.com/nickmckay/lipdViz) | Maps and plots |
| [agemodelR](https://github.com/nickmckay/agemodelR) | Age models (Bacon, Bchron, BAM) |
| [geoChronR](https://github.com/nickmckay/geoChronR) | Loads all four of the above |
| [compositeR](https://github.com/nickmckay/compositeR) | Compositing records into regional or global means |
| [actR](https://github.com/LinkedEarth/actR) | Shift and excursion detection |

::: callout-warning
## Old scripts may break
You need **lipdR 0.8.4 or newer** and **geoChronR 2.0.0 or newer**. lipdR 0.7 renamed the compilation fields (`inCompilationBeta` became `inCompilation`), added `filterByCompilation()`, and removed 27 functions. The old geoChronR (1.1.x) installs under the same name, so check `packageVersion("geoChronR")`.

lipdR 0.8 records the time scale (yr BP, ka, year CE, ...) of every time column, and gives every timeseries a standard `time` column. lipdViz, compositeR and actR use it by default, and take `time.units` to choose the scale, so records dated in yr BP and in year CE can be plotted and analyzed together. [Tutorial 1](tutorials/01-load-plot-map.qmd#time-axes) explains how it works.

lipdR 0.8.4 adds `filterByInterpretation()`, which selects records by their interpretations (for example, the records whose primary climate interpretation is precipitation), whichever number the interpretation has in each record. See [tutorial 1](tutorials/01-load-plot-map.qmd#interpretations).
:::
